domain_label: Monitored Training Loop, Checkpointing & Rollback (Fine-Tuning subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is the monitored training loop: eval cadence, early stopping, checkpointing, rollback, and lineage for fine-tuning specialist LLMs
base model already selected; data pipeline already constructed; focus is loop control and fault recovery
PEFT methods (LoRA, prefix-tuning) are in scope as the dominant fine-tuning paradigm
exclusions: data curation, deduplication, and preprocessing pipeline
RLHF reward model training (referenced only as a metric source)
privacy and regulatory compliance beyond audit trail lineage

competency_questions.question: What is the primary eval metric and what secondary guardrails constrain checkpoint selection?
How are offline eval metric gains reconciled with online user metrics before model promotion?
How frequently is the held-out eval metric computed during training and what drives cadence choice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VAL_CADENCE defines frequency and cost tradeoff

competency_questions.question: How is training instability detected between eval checkpoints without waiting for the full eval cycle?
How does the stall detection logic distinguish genuine metric regression from transient noise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STALL_DETECT defines smoothing and threshold logic

competency_questions.question: What triggers a rollback and how is the rollback target checkpoint identified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROLLBACK_EXEC driven by STALL_DETECT, target from BEST_MODEL_TRACK

competency_questions.question: What checkpoint fields are required to enable full resume, rollback, and PEFT adapter restore?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHECKPOINT_MGR + PEFT_COMPAT + RESUME_INTEGRITY define required state

competency_questions.question: How is the LR state preserved and verified after a checkpoint rollback?
How are neutral trailing steps identified and pruned from the run lineage?
How is the LR schedule configured to interact safely with early stopping patience?
What experiment tracking fields are required to reproduce a fine-tuning run and build the audit trail?
When is curriculum data ordering beneficial and how is it validated against the eval metric trajectory?
How are hyperparameter sweep configs selected without contaminating the early-stopping validation set?
What lineage fields must be complete before a fine-tuned model is eligible for promotion?

glossary.definition: held-out task metric (ROUGE, exact-match, reward score) used for stopping and rollback decisions
number of consecutive eval checkpoints without min_delta improvement before early stop fires
saved snapshot of model weights, optimizer state, and RNG state at a training step
restoring training state to a prior best-metric checkpoint after stall or regression detection
parameter-efficient fine-tuning method (LoRA, prefix-tuning, IA3) that trains adapter modules rather than full model weights
condition where the eval metric fails to improve by min_delta for patience consecutive eval events
secondary metric (toxicity, format compliance, perplexity) that must not regress beyond a threshold even when primary metric improves
immutable record linking a model artifact to its training run, dataset version, hyperparameters, and responsible engineer
the suffix of training steps after the best-metric checkpoint that produced no metric improvement

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for monitored fine-tuning loop work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Goodfellow et al. Deep Learning (early stopping), Huyen Designing ML Systems, Karpathy A Recipe for Training Neural Networks

nodes.definition: Select the primary held-out evaluation metric (loss, task accuracy, ROUGE, exact-match, reward-model score) that drives early-stopping and rollback decisions during fine-tuning.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task or benchmark changes signal metric revision

pros.claim: Anchors all stopping and rollback logic to a real task objective
pros.example: exact-match for code generation vs ROUGE for summarization

cons.claim: Wrong metric silently optimizes a proxy that diverges from user value

failure_modes: optimizing loss when task metric diverges
using single metric for multi-objective fine-tuning
acceptance_tests: metric produces non-trivially different rankings than loss on validation slice
metric documented with grade examples
revisit_triggers: task definition or label schema changes
primary metric disagrees with user-study outcomes

nodes.definition: Define how frequently the held-out evaluation metric is computed during training: every N steps, every epoch, adaptive schedule, or triggered by loss plateau.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU cost or dataset size changes

pros.claim: Frequent eval catches regressions early before wasted compute

cons.claim: Eval too frequent wastes GPU time on large datasets

failure_modes: eval so rare that regressions persist many steps
eval so frequent GPU stalls dominate
acceptance_tests: cadence validated against throughput budget
eval completes in <5% of step wall-time

nodes.definition: Implement patience-based early stopping: halt training when the primary eval metric fails to improve by min_delta for patience consecutive eval checkpoints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: patience must be re-tuned if eval cadence or LR schedule changes

pros.claim: Prevents overfitting and wasted GPU budget
pros.example: patience=5 stops run at best validation accuracy

cons.claim: Too-small patience halts promising runs during transient dips
cons.example: patience=1 stops at LR warmup noise

failure_modes: patience=1 triggering on LR warmup oscillation
no min_delta causing stop on numerical noise
acceptance_tests: stop signal triggers at true best-metric step not eval noise
best-model step reproduced from log
revisit_triggers: metric shows persistent plateau not noise

nodes.definition: Manage periodic model checkpoints: save optimizer state, model weights, and RNG state at configurable intervals; enforce retention policy to bound storage cost.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: storage quota or cloud cost policy changes

pros.claim: Enables rollback to any saved step; fault recovery without full retrain

cons.claim: Saving too frequently dominates I/O; saving too rarely loses recovery points
cons.example: 1-step save interval stalls training on NFS

failure_modes: checkpoint missing optimizer state (can't resume LR schedule)
retention deletes best checkpoint before rollback
acceptance_tests: resume from mid-run checkpoint matches loss curve of continuous run
best checkpoint not deleted by retention policy

nodes.definition: Execute rollback: detect stall/regression condition, load the best-metric checkpoint, optionally reset optimizer state or reduce LR, and resume or terminate training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: stall definition or patience policy changes

pros.claim: Recovers training value from a diverging run without full restart
pros.example: rollback to step 2000 after step 2400 regression

cons.claim: Rollback to wrong checkpoint loses genuine progress
cons.example: loading step 1000 when step 1800 was best

failure_modes: rolling back without optimizer state (LR schedule reset)
rollback loop cycling on noisy metric
acceptance_tests: restored checkpoint metric matches logged best-metric value
rollback event logged with step/reason
revisit_triggers: optimizer type changes requiring different state fields

nodes.definition: Identify and prune the trailing N training steps that produced no metric improvement (neutral suffix), retaining only the subsequence up to the best-metric checkpoint for lineage.

pros.claim: Reduces lineage noise and storage by discarding provably suboptimal suffix
pros.example: trim last 800 steps that degraded metric

cons.claim: Wrong best-step boundary prunes genuinely best model
cons.example: off-by-one on eval cadence prunes step 1800 best

failure_modes: pruning before best-step confirmed
deleting artifacts needed for audit
acceptance_tests: pruned boundary matches logged best-step exactly
original metric log archived before pruning

nodes.definition: Design the learning-rate schedule (warmup steps, decay type: cosine/linear/step) and configure it to interact correctly with early stopping and checkpoint/resume.

pros.claim: Warmup prevents early divergence; cosine decay smoothly anneals
pros.example: linear warmup 100 steps + cosine decay to budget

cons.claim: LR not saved in checkpoint breaks resume LR continuity
cons.example: resume loads step 2000 but restarts LR from peak

failure_modes: patience triggered during warmup before LR has stabilized
LR state not saved in checkpoint causing warm-restart artifacts
acceptance_tests: resume at step N reproduces same LR value as continuous run at step N
no NaN loss in first 100 warmup steps

nodes.definition: Monitor gradient norms, loss values, and auxiliary signals (learning rate, weight norms) during training to detect instability, NaN/Inf, or silent divergence before eval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logging backend or grad clipping policy changes

pros.claim: Catches instability before wasted eval cycles or diverged runs
pros.example: NaN gradient norm alert at step 150 before eval at step 200

cons.claim: Log volume dominates I/O on very large models

failure_modes: silent gradient explosion masked by clipping without alerting
loss looks flat but NaN in optimizer state
acceptance_tests: NaN/Inf detected and training halted within one logging interval
grad norm logged continuously and queryable
revisit_triggers: mixed precision mode changes numeric range

nodes.definition: Maintain a running best-model record keyed to the primary eval metric; update on each eval; distinguish best from most-recent for checkpoint retention and final model export.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: metric definition changes invalidating historical best

pros.claim: Ensures final model is best-metric not last-step
pros.example: export step 1800 not step 2400 after regression

cons.claim: Best-model tracking fails if metric changes mid-run
cons.example: changing from ROUGE to exact-match invalidates prior best

failure_modes: best-model record overwritten by worse checkpoint
metric sign convention flip (lower-better vs higher-better) causing wrong best
acceptance_tests: best model pointer reproducibly selects same checkpoint across two independent reruns
best-metric value logged with timestamp and step

nodes.definition: Design data ordering strategy during fine-tuning: random shuffle, easy-to-hard curriculum, domain-weighted sampling, or anti-curriculum; validate against eval metric trajectory.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain mix or difficulty labels change

pros.claim: Curriculum can improve sample efficiency and final metric on imbalanced data

cons.claim: Curriculum adds complexity with marginal or negative gain on balanced data

failure_modes: curriculum hides overfitting to easy examples
domain weighting causing metric to improve on seen domains only
acceptance_tests: eval metric with curriculum not significantly worse than random-shuffle at same compute
curriculum config logged with seed for reproducibility

nodes.definition: Record all hyperparameters, dataset versions, checkpoint paths, eval metric histories, and code commits for each fine-tuning run to enable reproducibility and comparison.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: experiment tracker API or schema changes

pros.claim: Enables comparison, debugging, and audit across runs

cons.claim: Logging overhead non-trivial on high-throughput short runs

failure_modes: hyperparameter not logged (can't reproduce)
dataset version not pinned (silent data drift between runs)
acceptance_tests: given run_id, all hyperparameters and metric history reproducible
dataset version resolvable from run_id

nodes.definition: Implement the detection logic that distinguishes a true stall/regression from transient noise: moving-average smoothing of metric history, threshold-based regression flag, and patience counter.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: metric noise profile changes with new data or architecture

pros.claim: Smoothing prevents false rollbacks from noisy eval metric
pros.example: EMA window=5 ignores single-step ROUGE dip

cons.claim: Over-smoothing delays detection of real regressions
cons.example: window=50 hides genuine metric collapse at step 800

failure_modes: smoothing window too long masking real regression
threshold too tight triggering on numerical noise
acceptance_tests: synthetic noisy metric with known regression detected within 2x patience window
no false positive on LR warmup oscillation

nodes.definition: Ensure checkpoint format, optimizer state, and resume logic are compatible with PEFT methods (LoRA, prefix-tuning, IA3): save only adapter weights, merge/unmerge correctly.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: PEFT library version upgrade or base model change

pros.claim: LoRA saves <1% of full weights; dramatically reduces checkpoint storage

cons.claim: PEFT library version mismatch silently loads wrong adapter shapes
cons.example: adapter rank mismatch after library upgrade

failure_modes: adapter merged into wrong base model weights
optimizer state missing adapter params causing LR reset on resume
acceptance_tests: adapter reload + inference output matches pre-save output on fixed prompt
merge produces numerically equivalent output to unmerged inference

nodes.definition: Define secondary guardrail metrics (perplexity, toxicity, format compliance, regression suite) that must not regress beyond a threshold even when the primary metric improves.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: safety policy or product requirements change

pros.claim: Prevents primary-metric wins that ship quality or safety regressions
pros.example: toxicity guardrail blocks run that improved ROUGE but increased toxic outputs

cons.claim: Too many strict guardrails block all checkpoints
cons.example: 10 guardrails each at 0.1% tolerance leaves no valid checkpoint

failure_modes: primary metric win accepted despite guardrail regression
guardrail threshold set so tight no checkpoint passes
acceptance_tests: guardrail regression blocks checkpoint selection even when primary metric improves
all guardrail thresholds documented with rationale
revisit_triggers: new capability introduced that affects guardrails

nodes.definition: Verify that training resumed from a checkpoint produces a loss curve and metric trajectory that matches a continuous run to within numerical tolerance, confirming no silent state corruption.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: distributed training topology or precision mode changes

pros.claim: Catches silent state corruption before it invalidates a long run
pros.example: resume from step 5000 matches step 5000-5100 of continuous run

cons.claim: Verification adds overhead; may be impractical on very long runs
cons.example: 100-step verify on a 100k-step run adds 0.1% overhead

failure_modes: optimizer state partially saved causing LR jump on resume
RNG state not restored causing different data order
acceptance_tests: loss at resume step N+1 within 0.01 absolute of equivalent continuous step
optimizer LR at resume matches LR formula at that step

nodes.definition: Configure the outer loop for hyperparameter sweeps (LR, batch size, LoRA rank) using population-based or grid/random search, with eval-in-the-loop selection of the best config.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: compute budget or search space changes

pros.claim: Eval-in-loop selection prevents wasting full budget on bad configs
pros.example: early-stop bad LR configs after 500 steps

cons.claim: Sweep overfits to eval metric used for config selection
cons.example: selecting LR on val set used for early stopping

failure_modes: sweep selection overfitting to the same val set used for early stopping
compute budget exhausted by sweep leaving no budget for best-config full run
acceptance_tests: best config selected on held-out subset not used in sweep eval
sweep report logged with all trial metrics and configs

nodes.definition: Manage multi-GPU/multi-node training loop coordination: gradient accumulation, DDP/FSDP sync, checkpoint consistency across ranks, and eval synchronization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hardware topology or framework version changes

pros.claim: Enables large-model fine-tuning otherwise impossible on single GPU

cons.claim: Rank desync silently corrupts checkpoint or produces non-reproducible metrics
cons.example: rank-1 saves partial checkpoint before barrier

failure_modes: checkpoint saved from non-rank-0 process without barrier
eval metric averaged incorrectly across unequal-sample ranks
acceptance_tests: checkpoint loaded on 1 GPU produces same inference output as 4-GPU training run
eval metric matches single-GPU run on fixed subset
revisit_triggers: topology changes from DDP to FSDP

nodes.definition: Maintain an immutable audit trail linking each exported model to its training run, dataset snapshot, hyperparameter config, eval metric history, and responsible engineer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: compliance requirements or model registry API changes

pros.claim: Enables post-hoc debugging and regulatory audit of fine-tuned models
pros.example: identify which dataset version caused regression from audit trail

cons.claim: Audit overhead increases with every new field requirement
cons.example: compliance adds 10 new required fields per run

failure_modes: exported model not traceable to dataset version
responsible engineer field missing for compliance audit
acceptance_tests: given model artifact, dataset snapshot version and training code commit resolvable
audit trail immutable after run completion

nodes.definition: Reconcile offline eval metric gains from fine-tuning with online A/B or shadow deployment metrics before promoting the fine-tuned model to production serving.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: shadow deployment infrastructure or A/B framework changes

pros.claim: Prevents shipping fine-tuned models that improve offline metric but harm users
pros.example: offline ROUGE up, shadow deployment user-rating down

cons.claim: Online tests slow and costly; add latency to fine-tuning iteration cycle

failure_modes: promoting on offline gain alone
offline and online metrics disagree in sign with no resolution
acceptance_tests: promotion blocked when offline and online disagree in sign
guardrail metrics non-regressing at promotion

edges.why_related: eval metric choice constrains how often eval can be afforded
edges.risk_of_conflict: cadence set without knowing metric cost
edges.example: ROUGE eval costs 10x loss; cadence must account
edges.resolution_rule: fix metric before setting cadence

edges.why_related: early stopping criterion depends on primary eval metric
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stopping logic targets real task objective
edges.risk_of_conflict: stopping on loss when task metric diverges
edges.example: patience on exact-match not on training loss
edges.resolution_rule: fix metric before implementing patience

edges.why_related: guardrail thresholds reference the primary metric
edges.risk_of_conflict: guardrails defined against different metric than primary
edges.example: toxicity guardrail added after primary metric change
edges.resolution_rule: fix primary metric before setting guardrail thresholds

edges.why_related: offline metric used for reconciliation defined here
edges.risk_of_conflict: online metric not aligned with offline definition
edges.example: ROUGE offline but user rating online without mapping
edges.resolution_rule: define offline metric before reconciliation

edges.why_related: patience counter steps measured in eval events; cadence defines event frequency
edges.risk_of_conflict: cadence change invalidates patience counter
edges.example: reduce cadence from 200 to 500 steps while keeping patience=5
edges.resolution_rule: fix cadence before tuning patience

edges.why_related: checkpoint saves often aligned with eval events to capture best model
edges.risk_of_conflict: saving every 100 steps when eval every 1000 wastes storage
edges.example: save only at eval checkpoints
edges.resolution_rule: align checkpoint interval with eval cadence

edges.why_related: stall detection operates on the sequence of eval events
edges.risk_of_conflict: stall detection runs off a different event clock
edges.example: stall counted in steps not eval events
edges.resolution_rule: use eval events as stall detection clock

edges.why_related: eval synchronization across ranks must fire at cadence boundary
edges.risk_of_conflict: rank desync at eval boundary distorts metric
edges.example: eval fires on rank-0 only, metric incorrect
edges.resolution_rule: barrier at eval boundary across all ranks

edges.why_related: early stopping signal triggers rollback to best checkpoint
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stopping and rollback are one atomic operation
edges.risk_of_conflict: early stop without rollback leaves model at worst step
edges.example: stop at step 2400 but serve last step not best
edges.resolution_rule: rollback must execute atomically on stop signal

edges.why_related: early stop fires when stall/regression detected
edges.risk_of_conflict: stopping without stable detection causes false stops
edges.example: patience=1 stops on noise
edges.resolution_rule: stall detection must precede early stop decision

edges.why_related: patience can fire during warmup before LR has stabilized
edges.risk_of_conflict: early stop during warmup wastes run
edges.example: patience=2 fires at step 80 of 100-step warmup
edges.resolution_rule: disable early stopping during warmup period

edges.why_related: rollback requires a valid checkpoint to restore
edges.risk_of_conflict: no checkpoint means rollback impossible
edges.example: rollback attempted but only checkpoint deleted by retention
edges.resolution_rule: never delete best checkpoint before rollback completes

edges.why_related: pruning operates on the checkpoint history
edges.risk_of_conflict: pruning before run ends deletes needed checkpoints
edges.example: auto-prune triggers mid-run
edges.resolution_rule: prune only after run completed and best confirmed

edges.why_related: resume integrity test requires the checkpoint to load
edges.risk_of_conflict: corrupt checkpoint discovered only at serve time
edges.example: integrity check not run after save
edges.resolution_rule: verify resume after every checkpoint save

edges.why_related: PEFT adapter checkpoint format differs from full-weights
edges.risk_of_conflict: adapter saved without optimizer state breaks resume
edges.example: LoRA checkpoint missing optimizer on resume
edges.resolution_rule: save adapter + optimizer state together

edges.why_related: rollback triggered by stall/regression detection output
edges.risk_of_conflict: rollback without detection fires on noise
edges.example: immediate rollback on single bad eval step
edges.resolution_rule: stall detection must confirm signal before rollback fires

edges.why_related: LR schedule must be restored or reset on rollback; ambiguity between resume-LR and reset-LR
edges.risk_of_conflict: LR jumps to wrong value after rollback
edges.example: rollback to step 1800 but LR reset to peak instead of step-1800 value
edges.resolution_rule: policy: restore LR to schedule value at rolled-back step

edges.why_related: resume integrity check should validate rollback correctness
edges.risk_of_conflict: rollback assumed correct without verification
edges.example: continue training from corrupted restored state
edges.resolution_rule: run integrity check after every rollback

edges.why_related: pruned run boundaries must be recorded in audit trail
edges.risk_of_conflict: pruning erases audit evidence
edges.example: delete all step artifacts before audit
edges.resolution_rule: archive metric log before pruning artifacts

edges.why_related: gradient norm monitoring catches LR-induced instability
edges.risk_of_conflict: monitor blind to LR state changes
edges.example: grad norm spikes at LR peak not correlated with LR log
edges.resolution_rule: log LR value alongside grad norm

edges.why_related: NaN/Inf detected by grad monitor may trigger emergency stop before patience fires
edges.risk_of_conflict: NaN not caught until eval fires and loss is NaN
edges.example: silent NaN optimizer state discovered at step 800 eval
edges.resolution_rule: NaN/Inf detection triggers immediate halt, not patience

edges.why_related: per-rank gradient norms need aggregation in distributed setting
edges.risk_of_conflict: rank-0 grad norm healthy but rank-3 exploding
edges.example: distributed run reports average grad norm masking per-rank explosion
edges.resolution_rule: log per-rank max grad norm

edges.why_related: rollback target is the best-model checkpoint
edges.risk_of_conflict: rollback to latest step when best is different
edges.example: step 1800 is best but rollback loads step 2400 latest
edges.resolution_rule: rollback reads best-model pointer not latest pointer

edges.why_related: best-step boundary drives pruning boundary
edges.risk_of_conflict: pruning before best-step confirmed removes best
edges.example: best-step updated after pruning removes it
edges.resolution_rule: confirm best-step before pruning

edges.why_related: best offline model selected by tracker is the candidate for reconciliation
edges.risk_of_conflict: reconciling a non-best checkpoint
edges.example: reconcile latest not best after regression
edges.resolution_rule: reconcile only the best-model checkpoint

edges.why_related: curriculum-ordered data may change metric dynamics; metric must account for ordering effects
edges.risk_of_conflict: eval metric valid only for random-shuffle
edges.example: ROUGE metric calibrated on shuffled data, curriculum produces different trajectory
edges.resolution_rule: validate metric trajectory with and without curriculum

edges.why_related: curriculum phases can cause apparent metric stalls at phase boundaries mistaken for true stalls
edges.benefit_of_coupling: none; requires stall-detection awareness of curriculum phases
edges.risk_of_conflict: false rollback at curriculum phase boundary
edges.example: stall detected at easy-to-hard transition; valid phase, not regression
edges.resolution_rule: disable or widen patience at known curriculum phase boundaries

edges.why_related: experiment tracker records feed the lineage audit trail
edges.risk_of_conflict: audit trail not updated from tracker
edges.example: tracker records local but audit requires central registry
edges.resolution_rule: sync tracker to audit trail at run completion

edges.why_related: sweep results logged in experiment tracker for comparison
edges.risk_of_conflict: sweep results not tracked, best config lost
edges.example: manual sweep with no logging
edges.resolution_rule: log all sweep trials with configs and metrics

edges.why_related: confirmed stall/regression signal drives rollback execution
edges.risk_of_conflict: rollback fires on raw metric noise
edges.example: rollback on single bad eval step without smoothing
edges.resolution_rule: stall detection produces confirmed signal before rollback

edges.why_related: rollback must restore PEFT adapter state not full model
edges.risk_of_conflict: rollback attempts to restore non-existent full checkpoint
edges.example: PEFT run rollback fails because checkpoint contains only adapter
edges.resolution_rule: checkpoint format must include adapter weights + optimizer

edges.why_related: guardrail regression can trigger early stop independent of patience
edges.risk_of_conflict: guardrail regression ignored until patience fires
edges.example: toxicity spike not acted on for 10 patience steps
edges.resolution_rule: guardrail breach triggers immediate stop outside patience logic

edges.why_related: guardrail metrics must be non-regressing at reconciliation gate
edges.risk_of_conflict: promotion on primary metric despite guardrail regression
edges.example: ROUGE up; toxicity guardrail failed but promotion proceeds
edges.resolution_rule: guardrail check required at reconciliation gate

edges.why_related: distributed resume integrity harder: all ranks must agree on state
edges.risk_of_conflict: rank state diverges silently after resume
edges.example: resume on 4 GPUs, 1 rank loads stale checkpoint
edges.resolution_rule: integrity check must verify all ranks loaded same checkpoint

edges.why_related: early stopping used within each sweep trial to bound per-trial compute
edges.risk_of_conflict: sweep trials run to full budget wasting compute on bad configs
edges.example: sweep without per-trial early stopping
edges.resolution_rule: apply early stopping within each sweep trial

edges.why_related: distributed training requires rank-0 barriers for consistent checkpoints
edges.risk_of_conflict: partial checkpoint from non-barrier save
edges.example: rank-3 saves checkpoint before barrier, data corrupt
edges.resolution_rule: require barrier before checkpoint write

edges.why_related: promotion gate requires traceable lineage before approving model
edges.risk_of_conflict: promoting model with incomplete lineage
edges.example: model promoted without dataset version in audit trail
edges.resolution_rule: lineage completeness is gate for reconciliation

edges.why_related: LR schedule is a primary sweep dimension
edges.risk_of_conflict: sweep ignores LR schedule type, only sweeps peak LR
edges.example: grid search on peak LR but all use constant schedule
edges.resolution_rule: include schedule type as sweep dimension

edges.why_related: metric must remain valid across curriculum phases
edges.risk_of_conflict: metric calibrated only for final distribution
edges.example: ROUGE calibrated on hard examples, curriculum starts easy
edges.resolution_rule: validate metric on each curriculum phase

conflict_axes.trigger: training loss decreases while task eval metric stagnates or regresses
resolution_order: switch primary stopping criterion to task metric
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: task eval metric dominates training loss for stopping decisions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: task metric regresses >2% absolute while loss drops >10%
conflict_axes.example: summarization loss down, ROUGE flat for 5 evals

conflict_axes.trigger: patience counter fires during LR warmup when metric is noisy before LR stabilizes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: warmup protection dominates patience during the warmup window
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: patience fires before LR reaches peak value
conflict_axes.example: patience=3 fires at step 80 of 100-step warmup

conflict_axes.trigger: aggressive retention policy deletes checkpoints needed for fine-grained rollback
resolution_order: set minimum retention window to cover patience window
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: best-metric checkpoint is exempt from retention deletion
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: best checkpoint deleted by retention policy
conflict_axes.example: keep-last-3 policy deletes best at step 1800 when latest is step 2400

conflict_axes.trigger: best offline model regresses online user metric or A/B metric
resolution_order: require online sign agreement before promotion
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: online outcome dominates offline metric for production promotion
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: offline and online disagree in direction
conflict_axes.example: ROUGE up 3pt, shadow deployment user rating down 1pt

conflict_axes.trigger: best primary metric checkpoint violates a guardrail threshold
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: guardrail constraints dominate primary metric gain when threshold exceeded
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: any guardrail regression at promotion checkpoint

conflict_axes.trigger: metric dip at curriculum phase transition triggers false stall detection and rollback
resolution_order: annotate phase boundaries in training log
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: phase-aware patience policy dominates generic stall detection at annotated boundaries
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: rollback fires at curriculum boundary confirmed not a true regression
conflict_axes.example: easy-to-hard transition causes 2-step ROUGE dip triggering patience

conflict_axes.trigger: validation set used for sweep selection is also used for early stopping, biasing both
resolution_order: use separate sweep-selection and early-stopping eval sets
use test set only for final reconciliation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: eval set integrity dominates sweep efficiency
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: sweep selection and early stopping use identical data split
conflict_axes.example: same 1k validation examples used for sweep config selection and patience

conflict_axes.trigger: rollback logic assumes full-model checkpoint format but run uses PEFT adapters
resolution_order: detect PEFT mode at rollback time
load adapter-only checkpoint with correct base model
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: PEFT-aware rollback logic dominates generic checkpoint restore
conflict_axes.example: rollback script tries to load full weights, fails because only adapter saved

conflict_axes.trigger: distributed eval aggregates metrics incorrectly across unequal-sample ranks, distorting stall detection
resolution_order: validate distributed metric matches single-GPU on fixed batch
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: correct metric aggregation dominates distributed throughput optimization
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: distributed metric diverges from single-GPU metric by >1% on same data
conflict_axes.example: 4-rank average uses unequal shard sizes producing biased ROUGE

edge_cases.trigger: patience fires during LR warmup before metric stabilizes
edge_cases.failure_mode: run terminated before LR peak, genuine training potential wasted
edge_cases.example: cosine warmup 200 steps, patience=3 evals fires at step 180

edge_cases.trigger: retention policy deletes best checkpoint before rollback is triggered
edge_cases.failure_mode: rollback impossible; must retrain from earlier checkpoint
edge_cases.example: keep-last-3 at step 2400 deletes step-1800 best
edge_cases.detection_method: check best-step in retained checkpoint list before deletion
resolution: mark best checkpoint exempt from retention

edge_cases.trigger: optimizer LR state not saved in checkpoint; resume restarts LR from initial value
edge_cases.failure_mode: LR spike at resume causes loss spike and false stall detection
edge_cases.example: resume at step 5000 but LR resets to peak 1e-4 instead of decayed 3e-5
edge_cases.detection_method: log and compare LR at resume step vs formula value at that step
resolution: save optimizer state including LR scheduler state
rebuild LR from schedule formula if state missing

edge_cases.trigger: adapter checkpoint loaded on different base model version than training base
edge_cases.failure_mode: silent wrong inference output; metric appears valid but model is wrong
edge_cases.example: LoRA adapter trained on Llama-3-8B loaded on Llama-3-8B-Instruct
edge_cases.detection_method: hash base model config and check against adapter metadata
resolution: store base model hash in adapter checkpoint metadata

edge_cases.trigger: metric sign convention (lower-better vs higher-better) set incorrectly; best model is worst
edge_cases.failure_mode: best-model tracker selects worst checkpoint; rollback makes things worse
edge_cases.example: perplexity treated as higher-better; highest PPL checkpoint selected
edge_cases.detection_method: unit test best-tracker on synthetic increasing and decreasing metric sequences
resolution: alert on first-eval vs baseline comparison

edge_cases.trigger: checkpoint saved without barrier; ranks save different step states
edge_cases.failure_mode: corrupted checkpoint; resume produces inconsistent model
edge_cases.example: rank-0 saves at step 1000, rank-3 still at step 998
edge_cases.detection_method: verify all rank checkpoint metadata agree on step number
resolution: require all-reduce barrier before checkpoint write
validate step number across ranks post-save

edge_cases.trigger: val set used for sweep config selection is the same set used for early stopping and final eval
edge_cases.failure_mode: inflated final metric; selected config overfits to val set
edge_cases.example: 500-example val set used for both sweep selection and final ROUGE
edge_cases.detection_method: require sweep selection val set disjoint from stopping and final eval sets
resolution: split validation into sweep-sel and stop-eval subsets
report final metric on held-out test set

edge_cases.trigger: metric dip at curriculum phase boundary mistaken for genuine stall
edge_cases.failure_mode: premature rollback to pre-boundary checkpoint, erasing curriculum progress
edge_cases.example: easy-to-hard phase switch causes 3-step ROUGE dip, patience fires
edge_cases.detection_method: annotate curriculum phase boundaries and widen patience window around them

edge_cases.trigger: experiment tracker records incomplete or not synced to audit trail before deletion
edge_cases.failure_mode: promoted model not traceable to dataset version or code commit
edge_cases.example: tracker log deleted after 30 days, audit requires dataset version
edge_cases.detection_method: verify audit trail completeness before model promotion
resolution: sync tracker to permanent audit store at run completion
enforce retention policy on audit store separately from tracker

edge_cases.trigger: training loss decreases monotonically while task metric stagnates or regresses
edge_cases.failure_mode: run continues past best task-metric checkpoint wasting compute and missing best model
edge_cases.example: cross-entropy loss drops from 2.0 to 0.8 while ROUGE-L flat at 0.42
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor task metric alongside loss; flag when they diverge in direction
resolution: switch early stopping to task metric

edge_cases.trigger: all checkpoints violate at least one guardrail; no valid model to promote
edge_cases.failure_mode: run produces no promotable checkpoint despite primary metric improvement
edge_cases.example: all checkpoints exceed toxicity threshold; primary metric improves throughout
edge_cases.detection_method: track per-checkpoint guardrail status; alert if all checkpoints fail
resolution: relax guardrail threshold with human approval

workflow.objective: define primary eval metric, secondary guardrails, and thresholds before loop config
acceptance_tests: primary metric documented
guardrail thresholds documented with rationale
workflow.do_first_because: all stopping, rollback, and promotion logic depends on stable metric and guardrail definitions

workflow.objective: design LR schedule and configure sweep space before training starts
acceptance_tests: warmup steps documented
sweep space documented
workflow.do_first_because: LR schedule interacts with patience; fix schedule before tuning patience

workflow.objective: set eval cadence and stall detection parameters (smoothing window, patience, threshold)
acceptance_tests: cadence validated against throughput budget
stall detection validated on synthetic noisy metric
workflow.do_first_because: cadence and patience interact; fix together to avoid warmup false stops

workflow.objective: configure checkpoint save interval, retention, PEFT adapter format, and verify resume
acceptance_tests: resume integrity test passes
best checkpoint protected from retention
workflow.do_first_because: checkpoint format must be locked before training starts to enable rollback

workflow.objective: configure early stopping patience, min_delta, rollback trigger, and rollback LR policy
entry_criteria: cadence, stall detection, and checkpoint config fixed
acceptance_tests: patience not active during warmup
rollback target verified as best-model pointer
exit_criteria: early stop and rollback config approved
workflow.do_first_because: stopping and rollback must be configured atomically to prevent rollback to wrong checkpoint

workflow.objective: wire experiment tracker and define curriculum ordering if applicable
acceptance_tests: all hyperparameters logged on run init
curriculum config reproducible from seed
workflow.do_first_because: tracker must be running before training to capture all metrics from step 0

workflow.objective: run training loop with gradient monitoring, distributed sync, and live best-model tracking
acceptance_tests: no NaN loss or grad norm
best-model pointer updated at each eval
rank sync verified
exit_criteria: training loop completes or early-stops cleanly
workflow.do_first_because: gradient monitoring and best-tracking run concurrently; both must be live before training

workflow.objective: prune neutral tail steps and build immutable lineage audit trail for the best model
acceptance_tests: best checkpoint not pruned
lineage traceable to dataset version and code commit
workflow.do_first_because: lineage must be built before promotion gate; pruning must not delete audit evidence

workflow.objective: reconcile offline best-model metric with online shadow/A-B result; gate promotion
acceptance_tests: online sign agrees with offline
all guardrails non-regressing
lineage complete
workflow.do_first_because: irreversible production promotion must be last; requires human review and all gates passed

priority_rationale.notes: tier=0 all stopping/rollback depends on metric
tier=4 PEFT format must match rollback logic
tier=5 rollback executes after all config locked
tier=5 best-model pointer required for reconciliation
tier=6 optional but must be configured before training

dominance_rules.trigger: offline metric improves but online or guardrail metric regresses
dominance_rules.rule: online outcome and guardrails dominate offline metric for promotion
dominance_rules.required_action: block promotion until online sign agreement and guardrails pass
dominance_rules.example: ROUGE up 3pt; shadow deployment user rating down; promotion blocked

dominance_rules.rule: warmup protection dominates patience; patience disabled until LR stabilizes
dominance_rules.required_action: disable early stopping for warmup duration
dominance_rules.example: patience=3 fires at step 80 of 100-step warmup; rule suppresses stop

dominance_rules.trigger: dependency order conflicts with value-first ordering
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence metric and cadence before patience and rollback
dominance_rules.example: do not configure rollback before checkpoint format locked

dominance_rules.trigger: retention policy would delete best checkpoint
dominance_rules.rule: best-metric checkpoint exempt from retention deletion
dominance_rules.required_action: exempt best checkpoint from any retention sweep
dominance_rules.example: keep-last-3 may not delete step-1800 best

dominance_rules.trigger: automation would make rollback without stall signal confirmation
dominance_rules.rule: stall detection signal must confirm before rollback executes
dominance_rules.required_action: require confirmed stall flag before rollback trigger
dominance_rules.example: single noisy eval step does not trigger rollback

dominance_rules.trigger: task eval metric diverges from training loss
dominance_rules.rule: task eval metric dominates training loss for stopping decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: switch primary stopping criterion to task metric
dominance_rules.example: loss down, ROUGE flat: ROUGE governs stopping

dominance_rules.trigger: sweep config selection uses same val set as early stopping
dominance_rules.rule: eval set integrity dominates sweep efficiency
dominance_rules.required_action: require disjoint sweep-selection and stopping-eval sets
dominance_rules.example: do not use same 1k examples for sweep selection and patience

dominance_rules.trigger: PEFT adapter rollback conflicts with full-model restore logic
dominance_rules.rule: PEFT-aware rollback dominates generic restore when PEFT mode active
dominance_rules.required_action: detect PEFT mode and load adapter-only checkpoint
dominance_rules.example: rollback script must branch on PEFT mode

dominance_rules.trigger: guardrail regression present at promotion regardless of primary metric
dominance_rules.rule: guardrail constraints dominate primary metric gain when threshold exceeded
dominance_rules.required_action: reject checkpoint; escalate to human review
dominance_rules.example: toxicity guardrail failure blocks code-accuracy win

dominance_rules.trigger: human review requested for irreversible or high-risk decision
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for promotion and high-risk rollback decisions
dominance_rules.example: promotion requires human sign-off even if all automated gates pass

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix eval metric and guardrail thresholds before configuring any stopping or rollback logic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: all stopping/rollback targets a metric; changing it forces reconfiguration
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: patience or rollback config references undefined metric
anti_rework_rules.example: configuring patience before deciding primary metric is ROUGE vs exact-match

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix LR schedule before tuning patience parameters
anti_rework_rules.rationale: LR warmup interacts with patience; fixing schedule prevents re-tuning patience
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: patience tuned then warmup steps changed requiring patience re-tune
anti_rework_rules.example: set patience=5 before learning warmup is 200 steps, then re-tune

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix checkpoint format and PEFT adapter format before training starts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: format change mid-run invalidates all prior checkpoints
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: adapter save format changed at step 5000; step 0-5000 checkpoints unloadable
anti_rework_rules.example: switch LoRA to full-finetune mid-run requires restart

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate resume integrity before long training runs
anti_rework_rules.rationale: discovering corrupt resume at step 50000 of a 100k-step run wastes 50k steps
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: resume tested only at run end after long training
anti_rework_rules.example: LR jump discovered at end of 3-day training run

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm best-step boundary before pruning any checkpoint artifacts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: pruning before best-step confirmed may delete best model
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: auto-prune fires at end of run before best-step logged
anti_rework_rules.example: best checkpoint deleted before audit; retrain required

anti_rework_rules.rule: wire experiment tracker before training starts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: metrics not logged from step 0 cannot be reconstructed for lineage
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tracker wired at step 2000; step 0-2000 metrics lost
anti_rework_rules.example: audit requires full metric history; only have step 2000+

anti_rework_rules.rule: lock stall detection config before training starts; do not change during run
anti_rework_rules.rationale: changing smoothing or patience mid-run makes rollback history inconsistent
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: patience changed from 5 to 3 at step 3000; prior rollback decisions invalidated
anti_rework_rules.example: mid-run patience change causes inappropriate rollback at step 3100

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve distributed training topology before checkpoint format decision
anti_rework_rules.rationale: topology change invalidates existing checkpoints and resume logic
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: switch from DDP to FSDP at step 10000; checkpoints incompatible
anti_rework_rules.example: FSDP sharded checkpoint not loadable in DDP resume logic

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete lineage audit before online reconciliation gate
anti_rework_rules.rationale: promoting unaudited model blocks regulatory audit and rollback
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: promotion gate passed before lineage complete; post-hoc audit fails
anti_rework_rules.example: model in production with no traceable dataset version

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate guardrail thresholds against baseline before training
blocked_until: guardrail thresholds benchmarked against untrained baseline
anti_rework_rules.rationale: threshold set too tight blocks all checkpoints; too loose misses real regressions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: all checkpoints fail toxicity guardrail because threshold set below baseline toxicity
anti_rework_rules.example: toxicity threshold 0.01 when baseline model is 0.05

anti_rework_rules.rule: run integrity check after every rollback before continuing training
anti_rework_rules.rationale: training on corrupted restored state wastes all subsequent compute
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rollback at step 1800 assumed correct; optimizer state corrupted; 5000 more steps wasted
anti_rework_rules.example: silent LR jump after rollback produces degraded model
